FIRST, THE ATTRIBUTION, because I dispatched you saying nothing further was
needed and I owe you the proof rather than a hunch. I compared the merge
product's tree against your branch tip directly:

  git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <your sha>   -> cf362563f
  git diff --stat <your sha> cf362563f -- kernel/ domains/ windows/
  -> EMPTY

Your sim trees are BYTE-IDENTICAL in the merge product. main moved 52 commits
since your base and every one of them is scripts/, docs/ or the Makefile --
three tooling merges. So there is no interaction to chase: both failures
reproduce on your own tip exactly as they appeared here.

FAILURE 2 IS THE MOMA, AT A THIRD SITE. windows/book/src/lib.rs:6028, and the
diff is one entry:

  expected  13 lines, including
            "In truth, the Moma's priesthood taught the darkening would come
             on day 35328; it came on day 35609 instead."
  actual    the same 12 lines without it

You removed two Moma lines from the reckoning[1] assertion around 5988 --
"numbers the darkenings: 81" and "taught wrongly" -- and kept "Among the Moma,
the sky has darkened". Correct, and your chronicle records why at 395-396.
But line 6035 carries a THIRD Moma line, in a DIFFERENT assertion, and nothing
touched it:

  $ git show <your sha>:windows/book/src/lib.rs | grep -n Moma
  5990:  "Among the Moma, the sky has darkened, now and again."
  6035:  "In truth, the Moma's priesthood taught the darkening would come..."

One world change, three assertion sites, two updated. This is the
five-witnesses shape the project keeps meeting: change what a thing contains
and every site that names it needs teaching, and the sites do not know about
each other. I raised the Moma consequence and read your chronicle answer and
still did not think to grep for OTHER assertions carrying the same string --
that is my miss as much as yours, and it is the cheap check we both skipped.

FAILURE 1 IS A PIN THAT DOES NOT DESCRIBE YOUR TIP.

  metrics.rs:14152   left (actual)   2.3846153846153846      <- = 31/13
                     right (pinned)  2.4

Your comment reads "refresh measured 2.4". Whatever that refresh measured, it
was not this tree: I checked whether any world-producing source moved after the
commit carrying the pin, and none did -- 0c4c2576d is both your last
world-touching commit AND the one that sets 2.4, and only a docs commit follows
it. So the pin and the world it describes are in the same commit and disagree.
The likeliest reading is that 2.4 was carried over from a measurement taken
earlier in the campaign; I can say with certainty that it is not what this tip
produces, and not why it was written.

WHY NEITHER COULD HAVE APPEARED IN YOUR GATE, which is the part worth changing:

  seed_42_name_syllables_are_pinned      baseline  15.593 s
  the_reckoning_renders_the_epoch_pair   baseline 136.409 s
  sub-floor roster membership            NEITHER

gate-commit runs only tests under the 1.0 s floor. Both of these are one and
two orders of magnitude above it, so no number of local commit gates would ever
have shown them to you. That is by design -- coverage is the stage gate's job --
but it means a world-touching campaign that only runs gate-commit is flying
blind on exactly the class of failure it is most likely to cause.

THE CHEAP CERTAIN REPRODUCTION, on your own machine, no box needed:

  cargo nextest run -p hornvale-lab  -E 'test(seed_42_name_syllables_are_pinned)'
  cargo nextest run -p hornvale-book -E 'test(the_reckoning_renders_the_epoch_pair)'

~152 s of execution plus your build. Take 2.3846153846153846 from the first
run's own output rather than recomputing it, and for the second, delete the
Moma line at 6035 -- your chronicle already carries the justification, so this
is the same ruling applied to a site you had not found.

I am not holding you for anything else. The census, the decision block, the DoD
and the disposition are all still good; nothing in this touches them.
